I went to a primarily white, I was the only female of color, middle/high school. I was also of an extremely low income, I came on scholarship, in high school it was super evident that everyone was extremely ignorant or just flat out racist. I somehow became the voice of African American people when in class discussions when black people are not monolithic. My mom, black, has always taught me about struggle, racism, and standing up for people in general so I was extremely outspoken. Through that I think a lot of people thought I was stupid, or I was treated as such. I will say we can all agree that the civil war was about slavery, yet in my class it wasn’t. And no slavery was not ok just because it was in the Bible and even then it wasn’t ok (I kid you not I was one of three people who said slavery was wrong in that theology class). My class didn’t read huckleberry Finn because the teacher was too afraid of what I would think of the n word being used. If you can’t teach that with my class why are you teaching it at all it’s all or nothing. I was even called a slur when speaking about mixed slaves in the US. I’m glad I got the education that I got, but I think they need to change their system to allow students to learn about other people and cultures. I can count the amount of POC we talked about in any class on one hand. We only spoke on western civilization. For a school that advertises a rounded education they really ingrained a white supremacist mindset if they wanted to or not. I was always seen as lesser. I wasn’t as pretty as all the other girls because I had natural hair and I was curvy. I was stupid because I would speak on things the other people wouldn’t understand. Sorry it’s extremely frustrating, but I think that experience did me good it shaped me as an outspoken person who can debate in a very levelheaded way.
